# Critical empty endpoint cuts retain a supporting-facet constraint

This note treats three full positive d-dimensional fibers A,K,B at
bases -1,0,1, where (A+B)/2 is contained in K. Assume d>=2. All
statements concern actual ambient caps, not independently specified
volume rows. They are necessary conditions, not an OC lower theorem.

Let y be in int K and let the through-source cap be

    H={ (z,x): u.(x-y)+alpha*z >= 0 },  u != 0.

Suppose its A capture is proper, with volume strictly between zero and
|A|, and its B capture has volume zero. Suppose further that H is a
local minimum of captured mixed volume under all small changes of its
normal that keep its boundary through (0,y). Global depth criticality
implies this hypothesis.

Write t_A=u.y+alpha, t_K=u.y, t_B=u.y-alpha. Let

    E_A=A intersect {u.x=t_A},
    E_K=K intersect {u.x=t_K},
    F_B=B intersect {u.x=t_B}.

For an ordinary section use sigma for its H_(d-1) measure and c for
its centroid. The first two sections have positive (d-1)-volume.

## 1. A support-face first derivative

Let L be a full-dimensional compact convex body, with u.x<=t on L.
Let F=L intersect {u.x=t}, allowing F to be empty. For any affine
functional v(x),

    lim_(epsilon down to 0) |L intersect {u.x-t+epsilon*v(x)>=0}|/epsilon
       = (1/||u||) integral_F [v(x)]_+ dH_(d-1)(x).       (1)

Here an empty or lower-dimensional F has zero (d-1)-measure. If the
original cut is strictly beyond the support, the cut remains empty
for sufficiently small epsilon and both sides are zero.

To prove the supporting case, choose orthogonal coordinates (r,s)
with s=(u.x-t)/||u||. Thus L lies at s<=0. Write
v(r,s)=a.r+b*s+c. For small positive epsilon the new inequality is

    s >= -epsilon*(a.r+c)/(||u||+epsilon*b).

All captured points lie in a slab -M*epsilon<=s<=0 for a fixed M,
because L is bounded. Fix r outside the projection of F into the
s=0 plane. Compactness gives a strictly negative upper endpoint of
the corresponding vertical section, when that section exists; hence
its contribution divided by epsilon tends to zero. For almost every
r in the relative interior of a full (d-1)-dimensional F, the vertical
section has upper endpoint zero and contains a nontrivial interval
below zero. The latter assertion follows by taking the convex hull
of a small relative ball in F with one interior point of L. Its
scaled length tends to [a.r+c]_+/||u||. The boundary of a full
dimensional convex F has zero (d-1)-measure. If F is lower-dimensional,
its entire projection has zero measure instead. Divided lengths are
bounded by M on a fixed bounded projection. Dominated convergence
proves (1). Orthogonal coordinates preserve the stated surface measure.

For a proper cutting hyperplane, the analogous signed derivative is
the integral of v over its section divided by ||u||. The same vertical
section argument proves it: for almost every point in the relative
interior of the section, the vertical interval extends to both sides
of the cutting plane; the exceptional relative boundary has measure
zero. Contributions outside the section vanish in the limit and are
uniformly bounded after division by epsilon. Thus this assertion does
not require smooth boundary or sections avoiding vertices.

## 2. The exact one-sided criticality inequality

Perturb u to u+epsilon*w and alpha to alpha+epsilon*beta. The affine
change of the cap margin at base z is w.(x-y)+beta*z. Applying (1)
at B and the proper-section signed formula at A,K proves that every
w in R^d and beta in R satisfy

    sigma_A * [w.(c_A-y)-beta]
      + sigma_K * w.(c_K-y)
      + integral_(F_B) [w.(x-y)+beta]_+ dH_(d-1)(x)
        >= 0.                                         (2)

The common positive factor 1/||u|| has been removed. If B's cut were
strictly beyond its support, the integral would be zero. Taking w=0,
beta=1 would then contradict sigma_A>0. Consequently a critical
zero B capture with a proper A capture must cut B at its support.
Taking w=0,beta=1 at that support gives the additional necessary bound

    sigma_A <= H_(d-1)(F_B).                           (3)

In particular F_B must be an actual facet of positive (d-1)-measure.
A merely lower-dimensional supporting face cannot supply a critical
zero endpoint capture opposite a proper captured endpoint.

Equation (2) retains the full distribution of points over that facet.
Replacing it by the scalar capacity (3) loses constraints on continuous
normal perturbations and on the section centroids. No free assignment
of supporting-face centroids is justified.

## 3. A section Brunn--Minkowski consequence

Since t_K=(t_A+t_B)/2, actual convexity gives

    (E_A+F_B)/2 subset E_K.

The three sets lie in parallel hyperplanes orthogonal to u. Translate
them into a common (d-1)-space and apply ordinary BM there. By (3),

    sigma_K^(1/(d-1))
       >= (sigma_A^(1/(d-1))+H_(d-1)(F_B)^(1/(d-1)))/2
       >= sigma_A^(1/(d-1)).

Hence sigma_K>=sigma_A. This inequality concerns actual sections,
not the captured d-volumes. It includes nonsmooth convex bodies.

The cases of a fully captured A fiber, or two zero captured endpoint
fibers, are deliberately not covered by the proper-A hypothesis.
They must not be discarded in a full critical-menu analysis. The
constant Gamma_d and an OC conclusion do not follow from this local
necessary condition alone.

## 4. Simultaneous zero captures give one actual enclosing simplex

Suppose exactly d+1 critical caps form a full-rank minimal positive
continuous circuit: their normals u_i span R^d and positive lambda_i
satisfy sum lambda_i*u_i=0. Suppose every B capture has zero d-volume.
Set D=sum lambda_i*alpha_i. Every point in int B has all its margins
strictly negative (a zero-volume closed cap cannot meet int B).
Their weighted sum is D, so D<0.

Multiply each margin by (d+1)*lambda_i/(-D). Write its new continuous
normal v_i and integer coefficient t_i. They satisfy

    sum v_i=0, sum t_i=-(d+1).

The linear map s -> (v_i.s)_i has image equal to the d-dimensional
subspace of vectors whose coordinate sum is zero: it has rank d and
its image lies in that subspace. Hence there is a unique s such that
v_i.s=-1-t_i for every i. The allowed fiber shear

    x' = x-y-s*z

fixes the integer coordinate and carries all caps simultaneously to

    v_i.x' >= z.

It preserves the mixed lattice and the d-volume in each fiber. In
these coordinates the B fiber is contained in the single simplex

    T={x': v_i.x'<=1 for every i}.

Indeed its affine barycentric map
lambda_i(x')=(1-v_i.x')/(d+1) is a bijection onto the hyperplane
sum lambda_i=1, and T maps to the standard simplex. The origin maps
to all equal barycentric coordinates, so it is the centroid of T.
This conclusion does not assert that 0 belongs to B or that B=T.

For every index whose A cut is proper, the actual face
B intersect {v_i.x'=1} is a facet with the capacity in (3), and its
Minkowski average with the actual A section at v_i.x'=-1 lies in
the K section at v_i.x'=0. Thus these supporting faces belong to
one body inside one common simplex; they cannot be chosen as unrelated
zero-volume endpoint cuts. For saturated A cuts, the proper-A capacity
lemma cannot be invoked. No global homothety or equality of section
centroids has been inferred.
